translation_notes: prefixes: BRICK->brick, SH->sh, VBIS->vbis, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, XSD->xsd, OWL->owl

15 .add() call sites on the single module-level `graph`: one @graph graph right after `graph = Graph()` designates it for the rest of the module, and every .add() becomes +{ }. Adjacent, unconditional, same-subject triples were merged with `;` (add_run_shared_subject shape) at each of the four spots where that happens (NodeShape+targetClass; PropertyShape+path[+pattern]); triples that switch subject, or that sit behind a further if/else, stay separate +{ } statements exactly where the original had a separate .add() -- no restructuring.

rdflib.collection.Collection(graph, listNode, items) builds an rdf:Collection (rdf:first/rdf:rest chain) via repeated low-level graph mutation; there is no island for it in the language (only single triple patterns), so it is left as plain Python, unchanged, same as the already-approved BrickSchema__Brick__generate_brick.py__define_relationships pair in this same stratum.

Context shim vbis_context.py restores get_brick_class, get_vbis_tags and rewrite_vbis_pattern verbatim from the source file's lines 21-57 (above the extracted region, which starts at line 62). vbis-brick-v5.csv is a hand-written fixture (the real file has thousands of rows) covering: one pattern, two patterns (SH:or branch), two full tags (SH:in branch), one full tag (SH:hasValue branch), a duplicate class (must be skipped), a blank Brick Class (must be skipped), and a class with zero VBIS tags (must be skipped) -- see driver.py.
